sources.title: Constantin Brancusi, Bird in Space (polished bronze, 1923-1940s series)
sources.relevance: Polished metal used to dissolve a subject into light and reflection; precedent for form-as-essence rather than likeness.

sources.title: Anish Kapoor, Cloud Gate (stainless steel, 2004-2006)
sources.relevance: A mirror surface whose subject is the surrounding environment and the viewer's distorted image.

sources.title: Narcissus myth (Ovid, Metamorphoses, Book III)
sources.relevance: Identity located in a reflection that cannot be possessed.

context_notes.note: Highly reflective sculpture tends to shift attention from object to surroundings; the image is mostly what the metal reflects.
Hard, single-source light and controlled black flags are the usual way to make chrome read as chrome rather than grey plastic.

interpretation.summary: The brief asks for absence rendered as material: a person known only through what a metal surface retains (contour, reflection, abrasion).

tensions.description: The figure must be legible enough to be missed, but never shown.

open_questions: Is the contour on the metal (sculptural) or in the metal (reflected)?

cautions: Sources are from model knowledge and were not opened in this run (verified=false).
Avoid direct imitation of a living artist's signature work.
